fields.meta_description: Build a lead capture form that holds junk for review and sends each lead to the right rep and your CRM. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Lead Capture Form That Hands Sales Clean Leads
fields.hero_description: Describe your offer and who follows up. Emergent builds the lead capture form, holds junk for review, assigns each lead to a rep and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After Someone Fills It In
fields.features_subheading: Most lead forms end at a thank-you page and an inbox nobody owns. These six pieces put each lead in front of the rep who works it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that change for known visitors

Hide the questions a returning visitor already answered and show the next ones in your list. A reader on a third download gives budget and timeline instead of an email again.
fields.feature_2:
Each lead assigned to an owner

Write the rule as a sentence, such as buyers this quarter go to a senior rep. Leads that match no rule join the monthly newsletter, and every assignment is logged on the lead.
fields.feature_3:
Junk held before it reaches sales

Hold submissions from throwaway inboxes and gibberish names in a review list. Reps see only leads a person typed, and anyone on the team can release a held lead back into the queue.
fields.feature_4:
Every lead synced to your CRM

Push each lead into HubSpot or Salesforce with its source page and campaign tags. A contact who comes back is updated in place, and reps never end up calling one person twice.
fields.feature_5:
The promised offer, sent on submit

Email the checklist or coupon the form promised as soon as someone submits. Each delivery is logged on the lead record, and a bounced address marks the lead as unreachable for sales.
fields.feature_6:
The whole codebase, exported

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repo when the form grows into a client portal. Your developers host it on their own servers and keep building without starting over.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Places a Lead Gets Captured
fields.tab_content_1:
Each download after the first skips the email field

Quillfield sells month-end close software and gates its close checklist behind a short form. A reader who comes back for the audit prep guide is not asked for an email again. The form shows two new questions instead, team size and current close tool, and both answers land on the same lead record.
fields.tab_content_2:
Sellers who list within 90 days go to an agent first

Copperleaf Realty's home value page asks for the address and when the owner expects to sell. An owner planning to list within 90 days is assigned to the agent for that neighborhood, and the agent gets a Slack message with the address. Owners further out get their valuation by email and a monthly market report.
fields.tab_content_3:
31 hot leads go out while the expo is still open

Kiteline Robotics works a two-day packaging expo with one form on a tablet. A rep types the visitor's name, company and production line, then taps hot, warm or cold. A hot lead goes to the account executive for that region in Slack the moment it is saved. By the end of day two the form held 212 visitors, 31 of them hot.
fields.tab_content_4:
Junk and repeat leads stay out of HubSpot

Lindale Solar's quote page drew 146 submissions last week. The form held 19 from throwaway email domains or with phone numbers too short to dial. Another 11 matched contacts already in HubSpot and were added to those records. The remaining 116 reached sales as new leads with the roof type attached.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Lead Capture Form
fields.howto_description: Settle the offer, the owner of each lead and what counts as junk before you open the builder.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the lead gets in return
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Mark each field required or optional
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the routing rule in one sentence
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for consent before calls or texts
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what happens to a lead once it is captured, starting with what the visitor receives: a checklist, a valuation, a demo slot or a discount. The offer sets how much you can fairly ask. A small download earns an email address, while a free consultation can earn a phone number and a timeline.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Count the fields you can act on and mark each one. Required fields are the ones sales cannot work without, such as a phone number on a callback offer. Make the rest optional, or hold them back for the second form a returning visitor sees.
fields.howto_step_3_des: State who gets each lead and how they hear about it, for example anyone outside the US goes to the partner desk by email. Name a backup owner for every rule, since a lead assigned to someone on vacation sits untouched until they return.
fields.howto_step_4_des: If your team will call or text the lead, add a checkbox that says so in plain words and record when it was ticked. Keep marketing email consent in a separate box, and store both answers on the lead record with the date.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Write the message the lead receives
fields.howto_step_5_des: Draft the confirmation email before launch. Put the promised file or link in it, say who will be in touch and roughly when, and sign it from a real person on the team. Use a reply-to address that someone reads every day.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the CRM and tag the source
fields.howto_step_6_des: Map each form field to its CRM property and send the campaign source with every lead. Tell Emergent which field decides a match, usually email. A repeat visitor then updates one contact instead of creating a second record.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Submit a test lead from a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Use a phone on a cellular connection and send yourself a lead. Check that the delivery email arrives, the right rep gets the alert and the CRM record shows the source page. Then send the same email again and confirm it merges into the first record.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is a glossary entry, a Pardot setup guide, a blog post on why these forms convert badly, two blank templates (Formsite, LimeSurvey), an event planner's help page and a Softr event form. Each one defines the form or hands over empty fields, and none shows what the form does with a lead after submit. This page covers four places lead capture actually happens (a gated download, a home valuation request, a trade show booth, a busy contact page full of junk) and shows the mechanics: a returning visitor asked new questions instead of the same email twice, a seller ready to list within 90 days sent to an agent first, booth leads rated hot before the team flies home, and spam and repeat submissions kept out of the CRM.
tab_stories: Quillfield, an accounting software company, gates its month-end close checklist behind a short form, and a visitor who downloaded something before is asked for team size and close tool instead of an email address again.

Copperleaf Realty's home value form asks for the address and when the owner plans to sell, and an owner listing within 90 days goes straight to the listing agent by text while the rest join a monthly market email.

Kiteline Robotics staff capture 212 visitors on a tablet over two days at a packaging expo, rate each one hot, warm or cold, and the 31 hot leads reach the right account executive in Slack before the booth is packed.
Lindale Solar's quote request page took 146 submissions last week, and the form held 19 as junk and merged 11 into existing HubSpot contacts, so only 116 new leads reached the sales team.
